mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances following a 2%+ MoM INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, increasing by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points in the month following the UNRATE trigger, indicating the labor market weakening is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both decline by more than 5% year-over-year, it signals a broad-based weakening of consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points in the month following the trigger, indicating the demand weakening is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over 3 months and payroll employment (PAYEMS) simultaneously declines by more than 100,000 jobs month-over-month, it signals a rapidly weakening labor market that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims (ICSA) decline by > 10% in the month following the trigger, indicating the labor market weakening is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% year-over-year, it signals a high-inflation, restrictive monetary policy regime that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate (T10YIE) rises by > 0.5 percentage points in the month following the trigger, indicating inflation expectations are becoming unanchored.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 2% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals a combination of supply shocks and restrictive monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances when both conditions are met.
